HasRecovered: N/A (no gap of 3+ months; single quiet month 2025-03 between the Feb 2025 Dockerfile commit and the Apr 2025 r2.7 merge)
Notes: Continuously active since 2019 with a declining volume: 2,251 commits in 2020 falling to 48 in 2025. The only quiet month (2025-03) sits between a Dockerfile contribution and the r2.7 release merge. Recent work is maintenance by the DLR team plus external PRs (Blender 4.5.7 upgrade, macOS fixes).

HypothesizedGapReason: Maintenance-only package. The last pre-gap commits (2023-01 and 2023-09) are CRAN release chores by the sole maintainer rCarto (version bump, NEWS, citation and URL fixes), followed by two small external PRs (#87, #88, Jan 2024). Only one issue (#89, Sep 2024) was opened during the 17-month gap, so there was no user pressure and no maintainer feature work; the riatelab team's development effort had moved to the successor package mapsf.
WhyRecovered: The one post-gap commit on 2025-07-23 ('update package, clean readme, fix urls, fix Rd links submit to CRAN') is a CRAN compliance release, not renewed development.
Notes: Steady 2015-2020, then only CRAN housekeeping. The 17-month gap (2024-02 to 2025-06) is easy to interpret: a finished package kept alive for CRAN by its original maintainer, with one external PR and one issue in two years. Not recovered in any meaningful sense.

HypothesizedGapReason: Single-author research code. All pre-gap commits are by Patrick Schaefer and are tied to papers ('latest research' 2021-09, 'Multivariate Extension for TEASER' 2022-03). Zero issues or PRs were created between 2021-10 and 2025-11, so there was no community to sustain it once the author's research moved on (his later time-series work is in other repositories).
WhyRecovered: The only post-gap commit (2025-05-02 'Update README.md') is a documentation touch-up, likely pointing readers elsewhere; no code changes.
Notes: Bursty research activity 2016-2019, then a 37-month gap (2022-04 to 2025-04) with a single README commit after it. Easy to interpret: academic code abandoned when the associated research ended, with no issues or PRs at all during the gap.

HypothesizedGapReason: Volunteer-driven data entry stalled. Pre-gap commits are catalogue additions by one volunteer (Andrew Tribick / ajtribick: PRs #1066-#1086, Jul-Sep 2018) merged by maintainer Hanno Rein. After issue #1087 (Oct 2018) no new PRs were opened until Jun 2019, so the maintainer had nothing to merge; the catalogue depends on volunteers and its main contributor paused.
WhyRecovered: New volunteers resumed submissions: PR #1088 (Jun 2019, Florian Cabot) and a burst of PRs #1089-#1094 (Nov 2019, Christian Sturm / Sol-d adding missing NGTS, KELT, WASP, HATS planets). From 2023 the recovery is sustained by 'Automated nightly update from oec_continuity' commits, i.e. the maintainer automated the data feed.
WhoRecovered: New people drove the 2019 recovery (Cabot, Sturm); the original maintainer (Rein) later set up automation that now produces almost all commits.
Notes: U-shaped: peak in 2013, trough in 2019 with a 6-month gap (2018-12 to 2019-05), recovery to ~300 commits/year. Moderately easy to interpret: the gap is the pause of a single prolific volunteer; recovery came from new volunteers and then from a nightly bot.

HypothesizedGapReason: Pause after a burst. April 2020 saw feature PRs (#22 IHW FDR control, #23 differential splicing) and a run of CI/Docker fixes by Johannes Koester ('patch docker daemon data root', 'try cleaning up cache'). With the features merged and CI stabilised, the two core developers paused for three months (2020-05 to 2020-07); open issues #10, #15, #20 were design questions, not blockers.
WhyRecovered: A user problem (issue #24, Aug 2020, template copy failing) prompted David Laehnemann to remove the oversized .test/report.html (PR #25) and fix a biomart caching failure (PR #26, Sep 2020); regular maintenance continued, reaching a bot-tagged v4.0.0 release in Oct 2025.
WhoRecovered: Same core maintainers (Laehnemann, Koester), later joined by release automation (github-actions bot).
Notes: Steady workflow with one 3-month gap in mid-2020 after an intense feature/CI sprint. Easy to interpret: a natural pause, ended by user bug reports. Still actively maintained by the same people in 2025.

Notes: Short, bursty history in WoC (2019-10 to 2021-07) from a two-person lab team, with refactoring and packaging work in Sep 2020 and a version bump plus an external PR (#15) in Jul 2021. GitHub shows a commit in 2026-09, so the project outlived WoC coverage; no real gap to interpret.

HypothesizedGapReason: Imported release history, not development activity. Pre- and post-gap commits are NOAO release snapshots by a generic 'IRAF' author ('IRAF PCIX Version 2.11.3' Dec 1999, 'IRAF DUNX Version 2.12.1' Jul 2002). The 30-month gap (2000-01 to 2002-06) is simply the interval between official 2.11.3 and 2.12.1 releases; GitHub issues/PRs did not exist for this period.
WhyRecovered: Releases continued (2.12.2 in 2004, 2.13 beta in 2006) and, after NOAO dropped support, the iraf-community project took over in 2017 to keep IRAF building on modern systems (bursts of 475 commits in 2017 and 744 in 2023). Recent commits add OpenSSL/TLS build support and merge the v2.18.1 changes.
WhoRecovered: New people: community maintainers led by Ole Streicher, with original NOAO developer Mike Fitzpatrick contributing merges in 2025.
Notes: Irregular with 23 gaps because the early history is reconstructed from release tarballs. The longest gap is an artifact of release cadence and was easy to explain once the author field was examined. Genuine recovery came from a community takeover in 2017.

HypothesizedGapReason: Single-author scientific package between versions. The last pre-gap commits (Nov 2018) add Python 3 support plus 'Automatic commit from generate_documentation.sh'; the only PR in the window is the author's own #2 'Dev'. With v1 complete and ported, there was nothing to do until the author planned a rewrite.
WhyRecovered: A full v2 rewrite: 'storing precession v1 documentation' (2020-05-18), 'wiping for v2', 'wiping gh-pages branch for v2', 'setting up actions', 'MIT license' (2020-05-27), followed by 220 commits in 2021 and 295 in 2023.
WhoRecovered: Same author (Davide Gerosa) plus a collaborator (MDM988) in 2020; by 2025 new contributors (Vera Eris Del Favero, Giulia Fumagalli) submit PRs #39, #40 that Gerosa merges.
Notes: Cyclical bursts every 2-3 years tied to versions and papers, with a 15-month gap (2018-12 to 2020-02) between v1 and v2. Easy to interpret from commit messages alone ('wiping for v2'). Recovered and still active with new contributors.

HypothesizedGapReason: Pre-launch placeholder. The 10 commits before the gap (all 2015-12-01, Nick Murphy) only rename README/LICENSE files and add a code of conduct; there was no code and zero issues or PRs. The 9-month gap (2016-01 to 2016-09) is the period when the project was being organised and presented rather than coded.
WhyRecovered: Oct 2016 commits add a citation to the APS DPP 2016 presentation and update project status; the first real code lands in Feb 2017 ('Very basic Plasma object', Drew Leonard) and activity grows to 5,367 commits in 2022.
WhoRecovered: Founder (Murphy) plus new contributors, starting with Drew Leonard and growing to 355 authors; recent commits are dominated by dependabot and lock-file bots.
Notes: Rising trajectory after a pre-launch gap in 2016. The gap is easy to interpret because the repository held only documentation files at the time. Recovery coincided with the public presentation of the project and the arrival of new developers.

HypothesizedGapReason: Internal development not pushed to GitHub. Pre-gap commits (Feb-Jul 2018) add BigMPI support and start a naming-convention refactor by giangiac; the first post-gap commits (Feb 2019) are 'Merge consistent-naming feature branch back into the development branch' with non-backwards-compatible API changes, showing the work continued on a branch during the 6-month gap (2018-08 to 2019-01). No issues or PRs were opened, consistent with a small Intel team working privately.
WhyRecovered: The refactor was merged (Feb 2019), a controlled-gate bug was fixed (Jul 2019), and a 'Major feature updates' commit introduced a CMake 3.15 build system (Dec 2019), leading to the 2020 burst of 299 commits.
WhoRecovered: Same Intel developers (jwhogabo, giangiac) plus a new contributor (Lee O'Riordan) in Dec 2019; since 2022 activity is mostly dependabot dependency bumps and merge commits.
Notes: Irregular: one development push in 2019-2021 surrounded by low activity. The 6-month gap is moderately easy to interpret from the merge messages that follow it. Recovered then, but current activity is largely automated dependency updates.
